title: Bronchoscopic Severity of Burn-Related Inhalation Injury: Mucosal Histopathology and Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) in Two Cohorts
content: Introduction: This study examined how the severity of burn-related inhalation injury assessed by bronchoscopy relates to tracheobronchial mucosal injury, early oxygenation, and ARDS. Methods: This observational study included two independent cohorts at the Vietnam National Burn Hospital. In the historical cohort (n = 45), histopathology was summarized by bronchoscopic AIS grade and serum cytokines (IL-6 and IL-8) by sampling period. In the contemporary cohort (n = 76), day-1 PaO₂/FiO₂ was summarized by AIS grade. Associations with Berlin-defined ARDS were estimated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Results: Among 34 patients with biopsies, median epithelial loss was 12% at AIS grade 1 and 65% at grade 4. Median submucosal thickness was 118 and 194 µm, respectively. Mean serum IL 6 and IL 8 concentrations were lower in available day-7 samples than in days 1–3 samples. Median day-1 PaO₂/FiO₂ was 226 mmHg at grade 1 and 111 mmHg at grade 4. Overall, 39/76 patients (51.3%) met ARDS criteria. The odds ratio per AIS grade increase was 4.29 (95% CI 2.23–8.26) before adjustment and 4.40 (95% CI 2.19–8.84) after adjustment for age and total body surface area burned. Conclusions: Higher AIS grades corresponded to greater mucosal injury and poorer early oxygenation in the respective cohorts and were associated with higher odds of ARDS after adjustment.
